headline: Love is not just an emotion—it's a biological state that changes your brain and body
universal_truth: Connection is not optional; we are built to bond
fun_facts: Love triggers the same brain regions as addiction—dopamine, oxytocin, and serotonin flood your system
Physical touch releases oxytocin, lowering stress hormones and blood pressure
Loneliness is as harmful to health as smoking 15 cigarettes a day
discussion_questions: How does knowing love is biological change how you think about it?
Why do you think evolution made love feel so powerful?
What forms of love matter most to your wellbeing?

hook.script: Love isn't just poetry and romance. It's chemistry. When you love, your brain floods with dopamine. Your body releases oxytocin. Your stress hormones drop. Love physically changes you. We're built for connection—it's written in our biology.

cliff.script: Why would evolution make love so powerful? Emotions could be subtle, optional. Instead, love hijacks reward circuits, creates physical dependency, and makes absence feel like pain. Why such intensity?
cliff.prompt: Why did evolution make love so powerful?

options.text: Strong bonds ensure offspring survival, pair bonding, and group cooperation
options.response: Yes. Evolution made love powerful because connection dramatically improved survival and reproduction.

options.text: Love was a side effect of other brain developments
options.response: Love's intensity suggests it was specifically selected for...

fact1.title: Addicted to Love
fact1.script: Romantic love activates the same brain reward circuits as addiction. Dopamine surges, creating craving and pleasure. New love literally creates an altered state—obsessive thoughts, euphoria, and withdrawal symptoms when apart. Love is nature's drug.

fact2.title: Touch Heals
fact2.script: Physical touch—hugging, holding hands—releases oxytocin, often called the 'bonding hormone.' Oxytocin lowers cortisol, reduces blood pressure, and promotes healing. Touch isn't just comforting; it's medicine.

fact3.title: Loneliness Kills
fact3.script: Chronic loneliness is as harmful as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Isolation increases inflammation, weakens immune function, and shortens lifespan. We evolved for connection. Without it, our biology suffers.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Connection is not optional. Love isn't a luxury or weakness—it's a biological necessity. Your need for love is as real as your need for food. Honor it. Cultivate it. Your health depends on it.

outro.script: That's Day 90—three months of learning together! Tomorrow begins April as we enter our month on technology and innovation. Until then, reach out to someone you love. It's good for both of you.

growTrack.title: Connection Cultivation - Love as Necessity
growTrack.learning_objective: Treat connection as a biological need, not an optional extra
growTrack.activity: Reach out to someone you care about today—a message, a call, a hug. Not because you have time, but because connection is a biological necessity. Notice how reaching out affects your own state. Love is mutual medicine.
